_note: Seven deep-coverage parks. Shape: Omit<Park, 'id' | 'updated_at'> & { sources: string[] }. Coordinates are the spring vent / swim area (USGS spring sites), not park polygon centroids. typical_closure_time is the local time the park TYPICALLY fills on summer weekends and holidays (from official 'often reaches capacity' language plus news/visitor reports) and must be labelled as typical, never as live. usgs_site_id = gauge at/for the spring; river_gauge_site_id = nearby river gauge used when the spring has no live series or for river-driven brown-outs; gauge_distance_km = distance from the swim area to river_gauge_site_id when set, otherwise to usgs_site_id. nws_grid/nws_zone/nws_county fetched live from api.weather.gov/points on 2026-09-19. Facts verified against official pages 2026-09-18/19.

parks.name: Ichetucknee Springs State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. to sundown, 365 days a year. Swimming (North Entrance): Head Spring closes 30 minutes before park closing; Blue Hole Spring and its trail close 1 hour before closing. Tubing (South Entrance): Dampier's Landing closes 5 p.m., tube rentals end 4:30 p.m., everyone off the river by 6 p.m. Midpoint Launch closed for repairs.
parks.fees: $6 per vehicle (2-8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle or motorcycle; $2 pedestrians, cyclists and extra passengers. Tube rentals are extra through the concessionaire (about $10-$35).

rules.alcohol: Prohibited on the river and anywhere inside the park.
rules.tubing: Year-round from Dampier's Landing (South Entrance) only; the north section is closed to tubing. Tubes up to 60 inches, no glitter; stay on your flotation device; no swimming from tubes on the river.
rules.pets: Not allowed in the water, on trails to launches or swim areas, or in vessels. Trestle Point and Pine Ridge trails are pet-friendly.
rules.life_jackets: Allowed and rentable; pool noodles are fine in the springs but not on the river.
other: Swim only at the Head Spring and Blue Hole - no swimming anywhere on the river.
No coolers, food, disposables, glass, speakers, tobacco or vapes, water guns, DPVs or large inflatables at swim areas or on the water (armbands OK).
Scuba at Blue Hole only, cavern or cave certified, two-diver minimum, done one hour before sunset.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard on duty - swim at your own risk. The spring water is about 72 F year-round, cold enough to tire swimmers quickly. Blue Hole is deep with a strong current and is for experienced swimmers only; the stairs can be slippery. The Blue Hole vent is a cave - diving is for cavern/cave-certified divers only.
parks.entrance_notes: Two entrances. North Entrance (8294 SW Elim Church Rd, Fort White) is for swimming at the Head Spring and Blue Hole - no tubing. South Entrance (12087 SW US Hwy 27) is for tubing from Dampier's Landing - no swimming. Entry is first-come, first-served; online passes do not guarantee entry or skip the line. When the park is full it closes to everyone, including pass holders; do not park and wait on the roadside - citations are issued. Third-party reports: arrive before 10 a.m. on summer weekends.
parks.description: A crystal-clear, spring-fed river in north Florida where you can swim at the Head Spring and Blue Hole or float the river from the South Entrance. On hot weekends and holidays the parking areas fill early and the gates close until space opens up.

parks.name: Ginnie Springs
parks.hours: Mon-Thu 8 a.m.-5 p.m.; Fri-Sat 8 a.m.-7 p.m.; Sun 8 a.m.-6 p.m. Day passes stop being issued at 3 p.m. and expire at sunset. Divers register by 5 p.m. (4 p.m. in winter).
parks.fees: Day admission: adults $25 (Mar-Oct) or $20 (Nov-Feb); children 4-12 $6 or $5; age 3 and under free. Certified divers $36; full-cave divers $28. Tubes $10 single / $20 double per day; snorkel mask or fins $8 each; life jackets free.

rules.alcohol: Open containers only inside campsites (policy effective Apr 21, 2026). Prohibited at the springs, decks, swimming areas, bathhouses and picnic areas. No glass bottles anywhere on the property.
rules.tubing: Float the Santa Fe River from Beaver's Landing to Twin Spring (about 1 hour), then a 15-minute walk back. Free air-fill station.
other: Every guest signs a waiver.
Visitors under 16 need constant adult supervision; campers under 18 need a guardian.
Snorkelers on the river must tow a dive flag or float (state law).
No solo diving; divers must register and sign the dive waiver.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguards on duty - swim at your own risk. The water is about 72 F year-round. Ginnie's springs open into the Devil's cave system: cave diving is only for certified cave divers, and open-water divers may not carry lights or enter any overhead environment (an iron grate closes the Ginnie Ballroom cavern after past diver deaths). Santa Fe River currents can be strong and the water dark after rain.
parks.entrance_notes: Private park at 5000 NE 60th Ave, High Springs (386-454-7188). Day passes can be bought online - encouraged but not required. Admissions are limited under the park's safety policy and late arrivals are not guaranteed entry; day guests park in overflow lots on busy summer weekends. Third-party reports say it rarely sells out, so no typical fill time is listed.
parks.description: A privately run springs park on the Santa Fe River with several clear blue spring pools, sun decks and stairs with railings into the water. Popular with snorkelers, tubers and cave divers; it charges per person rather than per car.

parks.name: Poe Springs Park
parks.hours: Open 7 days. May-Sep 8 a.m.-8 p.m.; Oct-Mar 8 a.m.-5 p.m. (April hours are not published). The spring and boat ramp close 30 minutes before the park. Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day.
parks.fees: May-Sep: $6 per vehicle, or $1 per person for walk-ins and cyclists. Oct-Mar: free.

rules.alcohol: Not stated on the county page - ask at the gate.
rules.tubing: Tube rentals on the river through the park concessionaire (Anderson's Outdoor Adventures).
rules.pets: Allowed on a hand-held leash at all times; pets may not swim in the spring.
rules.life_jackets: Not stated on the county page.
other: The park may close when the spring reaches its capacity of 100 people.
Scuba diving is not permitted.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard statement is published - assume no lifeguard on duty. Spring water is about 72 F. The spring pool opens onto the Santa Fe River, which runs high, fast and murky after heavy rain; the swim area closes whenever water clarity is poor. Entry is by concrete steps with a handrail.
parks.entrance_notes: Alachua County park at 28800 NW 182nd Ave, High Springs (352-264-6847). No reservations. The designated swim area has been closed since Jul 16, 2026 (poor water clarity; the spring stopped flowing during the 2026 drought); picnic areas, trails, the boat launch and paddling remain open. With only 100 people allowed in the spring it can fill late morning on summer weekends when open.
parks.description: A small Alachua County park where a spring pool meets the Santa Fe River, with a lodge, pavilions and a boardwalk through cypress swamp. Cheaper and quieter than the state parks, but the swim area closes whenever the river backs up or clarity drops.

parks.name: Ruth B. Kirby Gilchrist Blue Springs State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. to sundown, 365 days a year.
parks.fees: $6 per vehicle (2-8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle; $2 pedestrians and cyclists. Camping $18 per night plus fees.

rules.tubing: Not offered; rentals and concessions are unavailable during renovations.
rules.pets: Not allowed in swimming areas or the water (state park rule).
other: Snorkeling only in designated areas.
Registered campers may enter after the gate closes at capacity; day visitors may not.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard statement is published - assume no lifeguard on duty. Spring water is about 72 F year-round. The spring run is shallow and clear, but the Santa Fe River can back up into the springs and turn them dark after heavy rain.
parks.entrance_notes: Entrance at 7450 NE 60th St, High Springs (386-454-1369). No day-use reservations. On busy weekends the gate closes at capacity and does not reopen to day visitors until 8 a.m. the next day (visitor and county reports). Since Oct 29, 2025 there are no water activities while a new swim entrance, launch, bathrooms and larger campground are built - no reopening date yet.
parks.description: A group of clear springs on the Santa Fe River that became a state park in 2017, known for a wide, shallow run and easy snorkeling. The swimming area is closed for renovations until further notice; the picnic area and pavilion stay open.

parks.name: Rainbow Springs State Park
parks.hours: Headsprings (swimming) entrance: 8 a.m. to sunset, 365 days a year, unless closed at capacity. Tubing entrance: Memorial Day-Labor Day daily 8 a.m.-4 p.m. (last tram 4:30 p.m.); weekends only in spring and September (call to confirm); closed Oct-Mar.
parks.fees: $5 per vehicle (2-8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle; $2 pedestrians and cyclists. Tube rental and shuttle fees are extra, and the shuttle fee applies even with your own tube. Annual passes are sold on weekdays and non-holidays only.

rules.tubing: Not allowed at the headsprings. Tubing only from the separate Tubing Entrance (2-mile float, about 2 hours); tubers must be 5 or older, and ages 5-6 must wear a fastened life jacket.
rules.pets: Welcome in the campground; not permitted in swimming areas or buildings.
rules.life_jackets: Life preservers and noodles are allowed at the headsprings; required for tubers ages 5-6.
other: No inflatables of any kind (rafts, tubes, balls) at the headsprings.
Stay inside the buoyed swim area; snorkeling only inside the buoys (dive-flag law applies elsewhere).
No disposable food or drink containers on the river (aquatic preserve).
Private vessels must be carried about 1,800 ft from parking to the launch.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard on duty - all swimmers do so at their own risk. The water is about 72 F year-round. The headsprings swim area is 10-18 feet deep with no shallow end, so weak swimmers should wear a life preserver and everyone must stay inside the buoys. Paths around the springs are steep and uneven in places.
parks.entrance_notes: Three entrances. Main/headsprings (swimming) entrance at 19158 SW 81st Place Rd, Dunnellon requires a day-use reservation for everyone, including annual passholders, pedestrians and cyclists. Tubing entrance at 10830 SW 180th Ave Rd (seasonal). Campground at 18185 SW 94th St. When the headsprings reach capacity the park closes to all visitors and vehicles may not wait in line in the park or on adjacent roads. Parking lot renovation Sep 9, 2026 - Feb 4, 2027: limited parking. Third-party reports: typically hits capacity 9-10 a.m. on summer weekends.
parks.description: A first-magnitude spring near Dunnellon with a deep, clear swimming basin surrounded by gardens and man-made waterfalls from its roadside-attraction days. Reservations are now required for the headsprings entrance, and on summer weekends it still reaches capacity early.

parks.name: Blue Spring State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. until sundown, 365 days a year. Swimming season is April 1 - November 14; the spring run is closed to swimming and all water activities November 15 - March 31 for manatees (reopening can be delayed if manatees linger).
parks.fees: $6 per vehicle (2-8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle; $2 pedestrians, cyclists and extra passengers. Entry fee is collected online with the day-use reservation. Tube rentals extra (Blue Springs Adventures). Camping $24 per night; cabins $95 per night.

rules.tubing: Allowed in season; enter at the upper entry and float about 1/8 mile to the main swim dock. Inflatables over 72 inches are not allowed.
rules.pets: Pets - including service animals - are not allowed on the water.
other: No coolers, food, glass, speakers, tobacco, water guns or DPVs on the water.
No climbing the spring banks; no paddling in the swim area 10 a.m.-5 p.m.
Swimming with or approaching manatees is prohibited; no swimming after hours.
Scuba only in designated areas; open-water and free divers may not carry lights or go below 60 ft; 32 divers at a time; two-diver minimum.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguard statement is published - assume no lifeguard on duty. The water is about 72 F year-round. The spring boil is deep and leads into a cave system below 60 ft (certified divers only, no lights for open-water divers); the run has a steady current toward the St. Johns River. Manatees use the run in winter - never approach or swim with them.
parks.entrance_notes: 2100 W French Ave, Orange City (386-775-3663). Day-use reservations required since Jul 15, 2026 for everyone except campers and boat-tour guests; news reports put the daily cap at about 232 vehicle and 50 pedestrian/bike slots (estimate). The park frequently reaches capacity and may close for several hours; pedestrians and cyclists are not admitted while it is closed. Third-party reports: closed by about 10 a.m. on summer weekends.

swim_season.note: Manatee season Nov 15 - Mar 31: swimming and all water activities in the spring run are prohibited. Reopening may be delayed if manatees linger.

parks.description: A first-magnitude spring on the St. Johns River south of DeLand, famous for wintering manatees and a clear quarter-mile spring run for swimming and tubing. Swimming is only open April 1 - November 14, and day-use reservations are required.

parks.name: Wekiwa Springs State Park
parks.hours: 8 a.m. to sunset, 365 days a year. The swimming area is open from 8 a.m. until 30 minutes before park closing. Spring bathrooms may close briefly for cleaning; concession 9 a.m.-5 p.m.
parks.fees: $6 per vehicle (up to 8 people); $4 single-occupant vehicle; $2 pedestrians, cyclists and extra passengers. The entry fee is collected online when you make the day-use reservation (no extra reservation fee). Camping $24 per night plus fees.

rules.alcohol: Prohibited (stated on the park's picnicking page and F.A.C. 62D-2.014).
rules.tubing: Not offered at the spring; individual-size flotation devices are allowed in the swimming area.
rules.pets: Allowed on a 6-foot hand-held leash on trails and in use areas; not allowed in the swimming area.
rules.life_jackets: Allowed; not required. Children and non-swimmers must be with an adult swimmer at all times.
other: No diving or jumping - the spring is shallow.
No scuba, hookah or other tank-assisted breathing systems.
Swimming and snorkeling only in the spring - not in Wekiwa Springs Run, Rock Springs Run or the Wekiva River.
No grills, pop-up tents or canopies on the spring lawn.

parks.safety_notes: No lifeguards on duty - swimmers and snorkelers do so at their own risk. The water is 72 F year-round. The swim area is shallow (under 1 ft to about 5 ft), so diving and jumping are banned; the spring vent drops into a small cavern and scuba is prohibited. Children and non-swimmers must stay with an adult swimmer. Black bears and alligators live in the park.
parks.entrance_notes: 1800 Wekiwa Circle, Apopka (407-553-4348), off I-4 exit 94 about 20 minutes north of downtown Orlando. Day-use reservations are required for everyone, including annual passholders (since Sep 2, 2025); the daily number of reservations equals park capacity and same-day slots sell out on hot weekends and holidays. Ask the ranger station for a re-entry ticket if you leave. Campground construction may be under way (notice effective Jun 26, 2026).
parks.description: A large spring-fed swimming lagoon just north of Orlando, ringed by a grassy lawn for picnics and the start of the Wekiva River paddling trail. It is one of the few state-park springs with a swim lift and ramp into the water, and day-use entry now runs on reservations.
